checkpoints: "No error, plausible-looking similarity scores, but degraded ranking" is the signature of an embedding-space mismatch rather than a runtime bug - there is no exception or log to chase because cosine similarity always returns a valid float no matter which model produced the vectors.

Each embedding model learns its own coordinate space during training, so a vector produced by one model and a vector produced by a different model do not live in the same space, even when both happen to output the same dimensionality.

Cosine similarity computed between a query vector from one model's space and document vectors from another model's space still executes and returns an arithmetically valid number in a normal-looking range - that number simply carries no semantic meaning.

In this code, EmbeddingService (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) still embeds documents through the nightly reindex job, while this deploy wired SearchService to QueryEmbeddingService (all-MiniLM-L12-v2) for queries, so two different models feed vectors into the same column.

A dimensionality mismatch, meaning different vector lengths, would throw right at insert or comparison time against a fixed-size pgvector column; this bug stays silent specifically because both models happen to output exactly 384 dimensions, so no data-layer check catches the discrepancy.

The fix is to point search() back at the same embedding service used for indexing and remove the extra QueryEmbeddingService dependency entirely, so the index path and query path can never again be wired to two different models by mistake.

If the real goal is to finish migrating to the newer model rather than roll back, the entire documents table must be re-embedded under that model before both paths are pointed at it - a table can never be left holding vectors from two different models at once.

Validating the fix requires more than eyeballing a query: running a known paraphrase pair against its expected ranking confirms the model mismatch was really the cause, and measuring recall on a labelled sample after re-embedding confirms quality actually recovered.
